H1.text: Carry a bag up the stairs, or up a long ramp. Ride up a steep road, or a winding one.

H2.text: You end at the same height. So does gravity care which way you went?

H3.text: Aarav wants to ride to the hilltop. A steep path climbs sixty metres in just three hundred metres.

H4.text: The winding road reaches the same top, but it is one point two kilometres long. Where does gravity take more energy from him?

H5.text: By the end, you will know. And you will see why friction is different.

P1.text: So what is a conservative force?

P2.text: Gravity only checks two things. Where you start, and where you end.

P3.text: The path in between does not change its work. A force like this is called conservative.

P4.text: Friction is different. Every metre you slide, it takes away more energy.

P5.text: Its work depends on the path. A force like this is called non-conservative.

S1.text: Let's test it. A three kilogram box goes from the floor to a shelf, two metres up.

S2.text: Path one. Straight up, then across. Gravity does minus fifty eight point eight joules of work.

S3.text: Path two. Push it up a ramp, four metres long.

S4.text: Gravity's work is again minus fifty eight point eight joules.

S5.text: Path three, a staircase. Same answer again. Three paths, one finish line.

S6.text: Now slide it back down the ramp. Gravity gives back fifty eight point eight.

S9.text: Gravity points straight down. Only the up and down part of the motion counts. Sideways gets no work.

D1.text: Now the reason, step by step.

D2.text: Step one. Break any path into tiny steps. Each step has a sideways part and an up part.

D3.text: Step two. Sideways, gravity is at ninety degrees to the motion. So its work is zero.

D4.text: Step three. Going up by a tiny height, delta y, gravity does minus m g delta y.

D5.text: Step four. Add all the steps. The work is minus m g, times y two minus y one.

D6.text: Step five. Come back to the start, and y two equals y one. The round trip work is zero.

T1.text: Remember this. A conservative force does the same work on every path, and zero work on a round trip.

R2.text: One. Friction always points against the motion.

R3.text: Two. So on every bit of the path, its work is negative.

R4.text: Three. Negative bits never cancel. The longer the path, the more energy it takes.

R5.text: Four. So the round trip work is not zero. The energy turns into heat.

C2.text: Slide the box six metres, against ten newtons of friction. Minus sixty joules.

C3.text: The long way round is twelve metres. Minus one hundred and twenty joules. Twice as much.

C4.text: Now you try. Carry a bag up to the third floor and back down to the start. Total work done by gravity? Pause and decide.

C5.text: Zero! It is back at the same height. Gravity took energy going up, and gave it all back coming down.

C6.text: One more. A ball is thrown up and falls back to your hand. Is the total work by air drag zero? Pause and think.

C7.text: No! Drag points down on the way up, and up on the way down. Both bits are negative.

W2.text: Aarav and his bicycle have a mass of seventy kilograms. Air and road push back with twenty newtons.

W3.text: Gravity first. Seventy times nine point eight times sixty. Minus forty one thousand one hundred and sixty joules, on both paths.

W4.text: Now the resistance on the steep path. Twenty newtons times three hundred metres. Minus six thousand joules.

W5.text: On the winding road, twenty times twelve hundred. Minus twenty four thousand joules.

W6.text: Gravity does not care about the path. Resistance does, four times more on the road.

X2.text: Many students say a conservative force always does zero work.

X3.text: But it is zero only on a closed path. Floor to shelf, gravity did minus fifty eight point eight joules.

E1.text: Where is this asked? In one mark questions on conservative forces, and round trip numericals.

Q1.text: Exam level now. A two kilogram block is pulled up a rough incline, five metres long and three metres high, then slides back down. mu is zero point five, g is ten. Total work by gravity and by friction over the round trip? Pause and solve.

A1.text: The answer is A. Zero, and minus eighty joules.

A2.text: Gravity is conservative. The block ends where it started, so its work is zero.

A3.text: The incline has sine three fifths, so cos four fifths. Normal force: two times ten times zero point eight. Sixteen newtons.

A4.text: Friction is zero point five times sixteen. Eight newtons, against the motion both ways.

A5.text: Over ten metres, it does minus eight times ten. Minus eighty joules.

F1.text: Here is your recap. Screenshot this card.

Y1.text: Can you answer these three questions without help?

Y2.text: One. What makes a force conservative?

Y3.text: Two. Why is the round trip work of friction never zero?

Y4.text: Three. Why does gravity do the same work on the steep path and the winding road?

N1.text: Next time: a swing slows, stops and comes back. Where does its speed go? Find out in conservation of mechanical energy.
